name: goose
vendor: Block, now Linux Foundation Agentic AI Foundation (repo aaif-goose/goose)

surfaces.label: goose desktop app (Electron). Matched on the bundled Rust binary that the app starts as `goose serve --tls --platform desktop --enable-scheduler --host 127.0.0.1 --port N`, one per chat window, cwd = that window's working dir. NOT matched on the main Electron process (Goose.app/Contents/MacOS/Goose), whose Chromium helper children would always look like tool children. Bundle id is the Electron default com.electron.goose.

goose CLI in a terminal: `goose session` (alias `goose s`, interactive) and `goose run` (headless one-shot). One native Rust binary named `goose`; the agent loop runs in that process. The npm package @aaif/goose-acp puts a Node launcher (bin/goose.mjs) in front of the same binary, so match the native one. The name `goose` is shared with pressly/goose, a Go database-migration CLI (Homebrew formula `goose`, `go install`); its argv is a driver, a migration command or -dir, so those are in exclude_args.

Standalone `goose serve` (ACP over HTTP and WebSocket, default 127.0.0.1:3284). The desktop app's own server matches the gui surface first. Also `goose serve` started by hand or by a remote-access setup.
`goose acp`: ACP agent over stdio, started by an ACP client (editor or other UI) as a child process. Same native binary. Not seen in a real editor; from the CLI definition only.

working_signals.meaning: The developer shell tool runs in-process and spawns one `$SHELL -c <command>` child of the goose process per call, so a child of the goose process means a shell tool call is running. Blind while the model is streaming or thinking, and while a non-shell tool runs in-process. Over-reports if the user configured a stdio MCP extension (npx, uvx, a binary): those are long-lived children while idle. Default builtin extensions run in-process (duplex streams), so a default install has no idle children. Inferred from source; no running instance was observed.

UNVERIFIED and coarse. Every session of every surface writes one shared WAL database, so a fresh mtime on sessions.db-wal means some goose session persisted a message (user prompt at turn start, each assistant message, each tool response). It cannot be tied to one process, so the row has no per_session template and tools/agents_probe.py never evaluates this signal. A long model stream writes nothing until the message completes.
Weak fallback, inferred and uncalibrated. The Rust process should sit near 0 percent idle. Not measured because goose is not installed here.

waiting_signals.meaning: No hook and no OS-visible signal fires while goose waits on the human. Approve and SmartApprove modes (GOOSE_MODE, default auto) block in tool_execution.rs on a confirmation channel: the CLI shows a terminal prompt, the desktop gets an ACP session/request_permission request over its private WebSocket. MCP elicitation also blocks and is persisted to the session store as an action-required message (agent.rs ToolStreamItem::ActionRequired). The PreToolUse hook is emitted inside dispatch_tool_call, which runs only after the user allows, so it is not a waiting signal.

Desktop and `goose serve`: the pending approval exists on the ACP connection. Reachable only with the per-launch GOOSE_SERVER__SECRET_KEY the desktop app generates and passes to the server in its environment (a hand-started `goose serve` also needs it unless started with --dangerously-unauthenticated). Not read here.

hooks.config: Plugin-based, Open Plugins spec, shell-command actions. <plugin>/hooks/hooks.json inside ~/.agents/plugins/<name>/ (user), <project>/.agents/plugins/<name>/ (project, loaded when goose starts from that project) or goose's plugin install dir. Disable through `disabledPlugins` (docs) or `enabledPlugins` (source only) in ~/.config/goose/settings.json, <project>/.config/goose/settings.json or settings.local.json, or through the per-plugin `enabled` flag in the `plugins` map of ~/.config/goose/config.yaml (source only, keyed by plugin path). Actions run with `sh -c`, payload JSON on stdin, default timeout 30 s. Only type `command` exists. Applies to CLI and desktop because it lives in the agent core.

telemetry.how: Documented and in the default build features. Set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (e.g. http://localhost:4318) or otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint in ~/.config/goose/config.yaml. Traces, metrics and logs, OTLP over http/protobuf by default (gRPC only if built with grpc-tonic). Per-signal control with OTEL_{TRACES,METRICS,LOGS}_EXPORTER=otlp|console|none, OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true to turn off. Resource service.name=goose (override OTEL_SERVICE_NAME), service.namespace=goose, host.name, user.name. Spans follow GenAI conventions (gen_ai.*). Message and tool argument content only with OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=true. Nothing is exported when no endpoint is set. A GUI-launched desktop app does not inherit shell env, so use config.yaml or launchctl setenv.

notes: Nothing was observed running, so process shapes come from source, the release zip and the docs. Desktop: one `goose serve` per chat window, each hosting that window's sessions in-process; there is no per-session process and no per-session file, so a process maps to a session only by cwd (sessions.working_dir in the DB) or, for the CLI, by --session-id/--id (a new interactive session has no id in argv). `goose term init <shell>` exports AGENT_SESSION_ID into the user's shell, which is a shell-integration session, not the agent process. Session content lives in private conversations: never read messages. The most precise turn signals are configuration-dependent: the UserPromptSubmit/Stop hook pair, or an OTLP span stream. Without them, tool_children is the best OS-level signal and it is blind during model streaming. exclude_args is an exact argv match, so a value such as `-t list` or `-n list` wrongly excludes a real session; args_contain is a substring test: `serve` and `acp` as substrings also match a path containing them. Independent verification 2026-09-29: the shared executable name `goose` also belongs to pressly/goose (database migrations), which the original row matched as an idle agent; exclude_args now carries its drivers and commands, still an exact argv test, so a real session whose argument equals one of them (for example `goose run -t status`) is missed. path_contains `/.local/bin/goose` is a substring test on argv[0] and also matches `/.local/bin/goose-<anything>`. `goose term run <prompt>` (the `@goose` alias) runs an agent turn in a short-lived process and is excluded along with the other term subcommands, so it is not detected. Still nothing observed running, so confidence stays documented.
